messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming endpoints (us-west-2). p99 = 2.6s (baseline 0.9s). Cache miss rate for prefix-cache jumped from ~12% -> ~62% in last 15m. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/alerts/1769998888 :rotating_light:

samir: seeing it in traces — streaming tails stall on token emission not compute. p95 ~350ms up, p99 +1.7s. Most affected by requests with long prefixes (~>512 tokens).

joan: multiple customer-reports inbound (support ticket #24512, slack pm from @nebula-ai). They see trailing stalls / truncated streams. Not widespread but high-value customers affected.

tomas: correlated with prefix-hash rollout started ~1769997000. We changed the salt+scheme (v3 -> v4) and expanded namespace sharding. Suspect cache key reshuffle -> mass cold misses.

megan: can we quick rollback the prefix-hash rollout or toggle routing to prefer legacy cache? We should avoid full rollback if there's a softer mitigation.

samir: mitigation option A = set routing preference to legacy-prefix for streaming routes and warmback. Option B = extend cache TTL + warmers to reduce churn. A is fastest.

megan: agree. A then B. If A doesn't reduce p99 within 10-15m, rollback.

samir: command to flip routing (run on control plane):

```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/v1/route-toggles \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","prefer_legacy_prefix":true}'
```

oncall-rotor: I can run that now. Will announce in 2m and post results.

sre-bot: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T12:34:10Z stream-handler WARN key_lookup miss=1 key_namespace=prefix_v4 node=gw-12
2026-03-15T12:34:11Z stream-handler WARN kv_get latency=120ms key=...
2026-03-15T12:34:12Z router ERROR downstream=client timeout=3005ms request_id=abc123
```

oncall-rotor: ran routing toggle. Controlplane response: {"status":"ok","changed":true}. Will watch metrics.

joan: pulling customer-impact breakdown — p99 by tenant: nebula-ai 4.8s, acme-inc 1.6s, ~90% tenants unaffected. Nebula has multiple live streams this morning.

tomas: recommend canary rollback on nodes where prefix-v4 is active with lowest traffic first (10% of shard pool). That reduces churn while preserving rollout for others.

samir: also increasing prefix-cache TTL from 30s -> 300s as intermediate step. Command:

```bash
./infractl cache update --name prefix-cache --ttl 300 --region us-west-2
```

noncall-rotor: applied TTL change. infractl output: OK -> updated 6/6 shards.

megan: metrics update?

noncall-rotor: p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s in 8m since toggle + TTL. Cache miss rate down to ~28%. Still above baseline but improved.

megan: good. keep watching 30m. Create incident ticket (PM + postmortem) and schedule rollback if we see re-spike. I'll open postmortem ticket: https://pm.redwood.example/tickets/INC-1769998888

samir: next steps: 1) Hold rollout (stop v4 rollout), 2) run offline bucket-sim to compare v3/v4 key distribution, 3) plan controlled re-rollout with warmers.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Severity -> SEV2 (mitigated). Notifications: oncall and engineers subscribed.

oncall-rotor: handing off monitoring to tomas for the next 4 hours. I remain available for escalations.

tomas: will monitor tail traces and run canary rollback if any customer p99 exceeds 3s. If that happens, I'll coordinate full rollback with infra.

megan: thanks team — compile logs + tracing window and we'll run a short postmortem template after 24h. :thumbsup:
